# Avoro Brand Tokens

Avoro's canonical design-token package for frontend apps.

Published package: `@avoroglobal/brand-tokens`.

Preferred app import alias: `@avoro/brand-tokens`. Consuming apps can keep the shorter
`@avoro/*` import path by aliasing it to the GitHub Packages artifact, as Keystone does:

```json
"@avoro/brand-tokens": "npm:@avoroglobal/brand-tokens@1.1.1"
```

This package exposes Avoro Brand Identity v1.0 through three surfaces:

- TypeScript constants for application code
- a Tailwind preset for Next.js/Tailwind apps
- CSS custom properties for plain CSS or non-Tailwind contexts

Source of truth, and the only brand source this package should use:

- `/Users/sethcampbell/Documents/Claude/Projects/Avoro/brand-kit/brand-kit-no-investor/03-color/design-tokens.json`
- `/Users/sethcampbell/Documents/Claude/Projects/Avoro/brand-kit/brand-kit-no-investor/03-color/tokens.css`
- `/Users/sethcampbell/Documents/Claude/Projects/Avoro/brand-kit/brand-kit-no-investor/04-typography/README.md`
## Composition Rules

Tokens give you values. **`CLAUDE.md` at the repo root tells you how to compose them** — color allocation (60/30/10), the chartreuse invert rule, type rules, off-limits patterns (no gradients, no glassmorphism, no real-estate iconography), motion, and voice. Read both — neither is sufficient alone.

Claude Code reads `CLAUDE.md` automatically. If you use a different AI tool, point its rules file at this one:

- **Cursor:** add a `.cursor/rules/avoro.md` that imports the content of `CLAUDE.md`
- **GitHub Copilot:** copy to `.github/copilot-instructions.md`
- **Other / no AI:** read it as a contributor guide before opening a PR

PR review walks the nine-point rubric in `CLAUDE.md` section 10. PRs that break load-bearing rules (the invert rule, no gradients, no banned vocabulary) are blocked at review, not merged-and-fixed-later.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @avoro/brand-tokens@npm:@avoroglobal/brand-tokens
```

Use the registry configured for the Avoro organization. If publishing through GitHub Packages, configure `.npmrc` in the consuming repo before installing.

```ini
@avoroglobal:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com
//npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}
```

## TypeScript Usage

```ts
import { colors, typography } from "@avoro/brand-tokens";

console.log(colors.brand.chartreuse); // #C8E83D
console.log(typography.family.display); // Geist, -apple-system, system-ui, sans-serif
```

Primary exports:

- `colors`
- `typography`
- `space`
- `radius`
- `border`
- `shadow`
- `duration`
- `easing`
- `surfaces`
- `avoroTokens`

## Tailwind Usage

```ts
import { avoro } from "@avoro/brand-tokens/tailwind";

export default {
  presets: [avoro],
  content: ["./src/**/*.{ts,tsx}"],
};
```

Then use Avoro theme values through Tailwind:

```tsx
export function Example() {
  return <div className="bg-brand-chartreuse font-display text-neutral-ink">avoro/</div>;
}
```

## CSS Variables

Import once in the app's global CSS:

```css
@import "@avoro/brand-tokens/css";
```

Available examples:

```css
.button {
  background: var(--avoro-chartreuse);
  color: var(--avoro-ink);
  font-family: var(--avoro-font-display);
}
```

Surface mappings are included:

```html
<section data-avoro-surface="dark">
  <button style="background: var(--avoro-accent); color: var(--avoro-bg);">
    Continue
  </button>
</section>
```

On dark surfaces, `--avoro-accent` maps to full chartreuse. On light surfaces, it maps to `chartreuseDeep` for accessible type.

## Build And Test

```bash
npm install
npm test
```

`npm test` runs the build and verifies:

- TypeScript token exports
- Tailwind preset shape
- CSS custom properties
- ESM, CommonJS, and declaration outputs

## Publishing

The normal release path is the GitHub Actions workflow:

1. Merge approved token changes to `main`.
2. Run **Release Brand Tokens And Update Keystone** from the Actions tab.
3. Choose `patch`, `minor`, or `major`.

The workflow runs tests, bumps the package version, publishes
`@avoroglobal/brand-tokens`, updates Keystone's `@avoro/brand-tokens` alias, runs the
Keystone build, and opens a draft Keystone PR.

Manual fallback:

```bash
npm version patch
npm publish
```

## Updating Tokens

1. Update `src/tokens.ts` from the approved brand-kit source.
2. Run `npm test`.
3. Bump version according to semver.
4. Publish to GitHub Packages as `@avoroglobal/brand-tokens`.
5. Update consuming apps to point their `@avoro/brand-tokens` alias at the new version.

For Keystone, steps 2-5 are automated by the release workflow.

Semver policy:

- `patch`: fixes to incorrect token values or documentation
- `minor`: additive tokens that do not break consumers
- `major`: removed or renamed token keys, CSS variables, or export paths
